Interface ItemRef

public interface ItemRef
One item found by ItemSources, wherever it sits: a top-level slot, or inside a shulker box or bundle, any number of containers deep. Writes go back up the chain of containers to the top-level slot and mark its container changed.

Stale references never write. A ref checks, before every write, that its top-level slot still holds the stack it was found in and that no container on its chain has changed since it was read (a click, a command, another mod). If anything has, take(int) returns EMPTY and commit() returns false, with nothing written. Refs from one walk that share a container share its contents, so several takes in one walk stay consistent.

Server side only, on the server thread.

  • Method Details

    • stack

      net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack()
      The item. A top-level item is the live stack in its slot, so a change in place takes effect at once, stale or not; commit() only marks the container changed. A nested item is the walk's working copy: change it in place (a repair, a component) and commit() writes it back. Any later write through the same container (a take, put or commit of another item in it) writes it back too, so change a nested item only when it is to be kept.

    • take

      net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack take(int count)
      Removes up to count of the item and writes the change back. Returns what was removed, EMPTY when nothing was (an empty stack, or a stale ref).

    • put

      net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack put(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Puts stack into this item, when this item is a shulker box or a bundle, by vanilla's rules: a shulker box takes what may go inside a container item, merging into matching stacks before empty slots; a bundle takes what its weight allows. Writes back up the chain and returns what didn't fit, never changing stack itself. Returns all of it when this item isn't a container or the ref is stale. After a put, other refs from the same walk into this container are stale (a bundle's order changes), so walk again to read it.

    • commit

      boolean commit()
      Writes an in-place change to stack() back up the chain. Returns false, writing nothing, if the ref is stale.

    • depth

      int depth()
      0 for a top-level slot, 1 for an item inside a container there, and so on.

    • source

      ItemRef.Source source()
      Whether the top-level slot is in the inventory, the ender chest, a supplied container or a carried attachment.

    • path
